snapshot.statement:
Five workspaces share one Unity Catalog metastore, and by default every workspace can see every catalog. A new compliance requirement says one analytics catalog may be exposed to only two of the five workspaces, without splitting it into separate copies.

Which mechanism implements this?
options: Create a second metastore and replicate the whole catalog into it for the other workspaces
Grant USE CATALOG to the analysts group and rely on group membership per workspace
Convert the catalog's tables to external tables stored in a separate storage account
Workspace-catalog binding: assign the catalog to a restricted list of workspaces
snapshot.referenceTitle: What is Unity Catalog? — Databricks Docs

snapshot.statement: Security policy requires rotating the AWS IAM role that backs the company's lakehouse storage every quarter. The role is attached to a Unity Catalog storage credential that several external locations and external tables depend on. The platform team must implement the rotation without recreating objects or interrupting nightly pipelines. Which approach meets the requirement?
options: Create a second storage credential, then drop and recreate every external location and table against it during a release window.
Update the existing storage credential with the new IAM role, so external locations and tables keep referencing the same object.
Pause all pipelines during a maintenance window, rotate the role in AWS, and wait for Unity Catalog to rediscover the credential.
Create a new storage credential every quarter, because credentials are immutable once an external location references them.
snapshot.referenceTitle: What is Unity Catalog? — Databricks Docs

snapshot.statement: A platform team keeps its production notebooks in a Databricks Git folder cloned from the team's GitHub repository. External auditors must be allowed to open and read the folder's notebooks and run them on sample data, but they must not edit files, create branches, or push changes. How should a workspace admin grant the auditors' group this access?
options: Grant the auditors CAN RUN on the Git folder: workspace objects like Git folders use their own permission levels (CAN READ, CAN RUN, CAN EDIT, CAN MANAGE).
Grant the auditors SELECT on the Git folder through Unity Catalog, because Git folders are securables governed by the metastore like tables.
Grant the auditors nothing on the folder, because every workspace user can already view, edit, and run any Git folder by default.
Grant the auditors CAN RUN on the catalog's Delta tables, because permissions on a Git folder automatically extend to the data its notebooks read.

snapshot.statement: A production pipeline reads its database password from the Databricks secret scope etl-secrets. The analysts' group must be able to read an API key stored in that same scope, but the group must not be allowed to change the scope's access rules or overwrite secret values. How should the admin grant the analysts this access?
options: Grant nothing on the scope, because any workspace user can already read the secrets stored in every secret scope by default.
Grant the group SELECT on the secret scope through Unity Catalog, because secret scope ACLs are inherited automatically from Unity Catalog group privileges.
Grant the group the READ permission on the scope's ACL: READ allows reading secret values, and only MANAGE can change the scope's permissions.
Grant the group MANAGE on the scope, because MANAGE is the permission level that lets principals read secret values.
snapshot.referenceTitle: Manage secrets — Databricks Docs

snapshot.statement: A contractor's engagement ends today, and the offboarding checklist requires that all access to Unity Catalog data be cut off before the end of the day. An access review confirms that the contractor's privileges on dozens of tables all arrive through membership in three groups; the contractor holds no direct grants. Which action cuts off the contractor's data access completely and verifiably?
options: Revoke SELECT from each of the three groups on every table they can currently read, working through the dozens of objects one by one before the end of the day.
Wait for the contractor's personal access tokens to expire, which automatically disables the account's data access.
Rename the contractor's user account so that sign-in fails, and leave the group memberships and all grants exactly as they are.
Remove the contractor from the three groups: every privilege arrived through membership, so this single change cuts off all table access and is auditable.
snapshot.referenceTitle: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog — Databricks Docs

snapshot.statement: A global company syncs its Databricks groups from its identity provider using automatic identity management. The group data-latam is a nested member of the corporate group data-global, which holds SELECT on the catalog analytics. A data engineer whose only group is data-latam runs a query against a table in analytics. What happens?
options: The query fails: Databricks groups cannot be nested, so data-latam would have to be flattened into data-global before any grant can apply.
The query succeeds: members of nested groups inherit the parent's permissions, so the SELECT granted to data-global applies to data-latam's members.
The query fails: privileges granted to a group apply only to the users and service principals listed as its direct members.
The query succeeds, but only because Unity Catalog automatically duplicates the parent's grant onto every child group at the moment the nesting is created.
snapshot.referenceTitle: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog — Databricks Docs

snapshot.statement:
Finance needs a monthly cost breakdown of Databricks usage by team for chargeback, computed from the lakehouse itself rather than from invoices or the cloud provider's console.

Which approach meets this?
options: Query system.billing.usage, filtering by workspace and tags, aggregating DBUs and dollars per team
Parse the monthly PDF invoices with a notebook and load the results into a Delta table
Read the cloud provider's billing export, which already itemizes Databricks DBUs per team and workspace
Enable a workspace setting that emails each team leader their DBU total every month

snapshot.statement: A company runs one Unity Catalog metastore shared by several business domains. Security policy requires that every managed table created in the finance catalog keeps its data files under a storage prefix dedicated to finance (s3://acme-managed/finance/), instead of the metastore root storage used by other domains. How should the platform team configure this?
options: Spin up a second metastore whose root storage is the finance prefix, because managed storage locations exist only at the metastore level.
Leave the catalog as it is, because managed tables in every catalog are always written to the metastore's root storage location and can never use anything else.
Create the finance catalog with MANAGED LOCATION 's3://acme-managed/finance/', overriding the metastore root storage for that catalog's managed tables.
Create the finance tables as external tables with LOCATION under the finance prefix, because managed locations per catalog work only with external tables.

snapshot.statement: During an architecture review, a new data engineer must explain how three Unity Catalog objects work together for cloud storage: the object that holds the IAM credential, the object that registers a storage path for external tables, and the object that gives notebooks governed access to files. Which explanation is correct?
options: Volumes have replaced external locations entirely, so a single volume type now covers both the registration of storage paths for tables and practical access to files.
Storage credentials point to the catalogs that use them and carry the privilege to run queries against those catalogs.
External locations store the IAM credentials of every external table registered under them, one credential per table.
Storage credentials hold the IAM credential, external locations register a storage path referencing it, and volumes give governed access to files.

snapshot.statement: A Lakeflow Job writes manifest files directly to the cloud storage path s3://acme-dropzone/manifests/, which is registered in Unity Catalog as the external location acme_dropzone. The job runs under the service principal loader-sp and does not write through any table or volume. Which grant authorizes the job's writes?
options: Grant the service principal WRITE FILES on the external location acme_dropzone, which authorizes direct writes on the registered path.
Grant the service principal SELECT on the external location acme_dropzone, which is the standard read privilege for governed data objects.
Grant the service principal WRITE VOLUME on the external location acme_dropzone, because volume privileges cover its registered storage paths.
Grant the service principal nothing, because Unity Catalog cannot authorize direct writes to a storage path outside tables and volumes.
snapshot.referenceTitle: Manage privileges in Unity Catalog — Databricks Docs

snapshot.statement: During a security review, an auditor asks what the Databricks audit trail actually captures, expecting it to log only SQL queries. The platform lead must answer based on the documented coverage of the audit log system table (system.access.audit). Which answer is accurate?
options: Only SELECT statements are captured; every other kind of event, including permission changes and object creation, is out of the audit trail's scope.
Only sign-in events are captured; queries run against the lakehouse are recorded solely in query history, never in audit logs.
A broad range of events is captured: logins and logouts, queries, permission changes such as grants, and object changes, each with the acting principal and timestamp.
Permission changes are not captured; audit events record queries and logins but never grants or revokes on governed objects.
